news.title: Show HN: Things to Do API
news.description: I built an api/mcp for local events: pop-ups, one-off events, concerts, etc. currently covering the SF bay area. I've been building a bunch of consumer apps lately around personalization and recommendation and have had a hard time finding this data in one spot. agents can find useful stuff through tool calls / web search, but slow. you can scrape on demand too, but i wanted a faster data set and couldn't find an existing provider for the mix of event types I was searching for. the methodology for it is to find influential accounts/posters/etc. and do a fan out across things that they co-post with. mcp: `claude mcp add --transport http thingstodo https://api.thingstodoapi.com/mcp ` I'm considering adding other cities. If you're building something that needs local event data, would something like this be useful and where would you want coverage? news.title: Show HN: Esp32sim – Run ESP32 firmware in the browser
news.description: Hi HN, I’ve been working on esp32sim, an open-source ESP32 emulator that runs in the browser. The fun part of the demo is that there is no ESP32 involved — the firmware is executing in the emulator. The goal is to make ESP32 software easier to experiment with, test and simulate without always needing physical hardware connected. Source: https://github.com/mikroverk/esp32sim I made a short video showing it in action: https://youtu.be/waoWFilTWEc I’m particularly interested in feedback from embedded developers: what would an emulator like this need to support before you’d actually use it for development, testing or CI?
